correctness.rationale: Final claim audited: a six-edge maximal matching leaves a nonincident point and line, and the count d of matching edges between their two neighborhoods is a complete full-automorphism invariant. For a fixed nonincident pair, the binary plane splits as ker(lambda) plus the span of the unmatched point p. On the three nonzero vectors x_i of the kernel and their translates p+x_i, the remaining line forms separate into y_i and y_i+lambda. Only x_i and p+x_i can use y_i after deleting the two unmatched vertices. Choosing x_i–y_i for i in D forces exactly a fixed-point-free permutation on D for the unmatched translated points and shifted forms; outside D the choices are forced. Thus d=0,2,3 gives 1,3,2 completions per pair. The pair stabilizer contains the entire S_3 acting on these three vectors and conjugating their derangements, hence is transitive within each type. The incidence count is preserved even by graph automorphisms interchanging vertex types, so no full-group orbit can merge two types; 28 nonincident pairs give orbit sizes 28,84,56. By invariance of the priority law each orbit has constant weight. The three known distinct size-six weight classes have exactly those distinct multiplicities, so the assignment of weights to orbit types follows. A separate replay enumerating all bijections on remaining vertices confirmed all 28 residual matchings censuses and the representative weights. The frozen broader law was also confirmed by forwarding exact rational mass through each partial labelled matching and explicitly generating 336 binary-plane graph automorphisms; it was not rejected for a numerical error.
residual_risks: The repaired structural theorem classifies only size-six maximal matchings. The probability identification requires an automorphism-invariant priority law for constancy and the specified i.i.d. continuous law for the listed weights.

value.rationale: The valuable remainder explains why three equiprobability classes occur at the same terminal occupancy and supplies a graph-local way to tell them apart. Six dimers are the unique near-perfect case, naturally leaving exactly one point and one line, so the fixed-pair completion problem is intrinsic rather than a parameter slice invented from the table. A researcher can now determine the orbit and read off the already known deposition weight from a single neighborhood-edge count, without enumerating matchings, automorphisms or histories. The explicit derangement model also describes all completions of any fixed uncovered pair. The original numerical recomputation is not the basis for this value finding.
residual_risks: No corresponding orbit classifier for larger incidence planes or other graph symmetries is claimed.
